learn.title: Ready-made helpers
learn.body: The header `string.h` offers functions that work on whole strings: `strlen` for length, `strcmp` to compare, `strcpy` to copy and `strcat` to join. You write `#include` with `string.h` to use them.

learn.title: Length and size
learn.body: `strlen(s)` counts characters before the terminator, so it gives 3 for "cat". `sizeof s` counts every byte of the array, 4. The two answers differ.

learn.title: Comparing strings
learn.body: `strcmp(a, b)` returns 0 if they are equal, a negative number if `a` comes first alphabetically, a positive one if `a` comes later. Only the sign is promised.

learn.title: Why == fails
learn.body: `a == b` compares the two arrays' addresses, not their text. Two separate arrays are at different places, so it gives 0 even for equal text. Use `strcmp`.

learn.title: Copy and join
learn.body: `strcpy` copies text over the start of an array and `strcat` adds text to the end. The destination must be big enough, or you write past its end. Here 20 bytes is plenty.

learn.title: Read a strcmp result
steps: Look at the first letters: `a` and `b`
Reverse the arguments and it is positive

learn.body: Before `strcpy` or `strcat`, make sure the destination has room for the text plus the terminator.
